name: delta_pm25
source_detail: COMEAP (2010), section 4.1, printed p.38: frames the policy question as a sustained reduction of 1 ug/m3 PM2.5
note: ASSUMPTION: the hypothetical intervention that defines the question. Permanent and borough-wide, starting in year 1.

name: hr_per_10ugm3
source_detail: COMEAP statement (January 2022, published 16 March 2022), p.8 para 31: summary estimate 1.08 (95% CI 1.06, 1.09) per 10 ug/m3, from Chen and Hoek (2020)
note: Applied as HR^(-delta/10) to all-cause mortality; linear on the log scale with no cut-off (p.13 para 50(iii)). Fingertips 93861 uses the same 1.08, confirmed by the validation test.

name: hr_log_se
note: The published interval is slightly asymmetric on the log scale, so the drawn 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles differ a little from 1.06 and 1.09 (outputs/psa_hr_check.csv).

name: lag_share_year1
source_detail: COMEAP statement (2022), p.11 para 40: US EPA cessation lag, 30% of the risk reduction in the first year
note: Cumulative share in force: 30% in year 1.

name: lag_share_years2_5
source_detail: COMEAP statement (2022), p.11 para 40: 50% across years 2 to 5 (12.5% a year)
note: Cumulative 42.5%, 55%, 67.5% and 80% in years 2 to 5.

name: lag_share_years6_20
source_detail: COMEAP statement (2022) p.11 para 40: remaining 20% across years 6 to 20 with smoothed annual values; COMEAP (2010) cessation lag paper, Table 17, p.52: 1.33% a year
note: Spread evenly at 20/15 = 1.333% a year, reaching 100% in year 20. Scenario: no lag (100% from year 1).

name: age_min
source_detail: COMEAP (2010), section 3.1.2, printed p.31: reduced hazards applied from age 30; Fingertips 93861 counts deaths at ages 30 and over
note: Only people aged 30 and over gain in the model.

name: age_max
source_detail: ONS National life tables, England 2022-2024: ages 0 to 100
note: ASSUMPTION: follow-up stops after the year lived at age 100; survival past 100 is ignored, a small underestimate.

name: population_year
source_detail: ONS mid-year population estimates via Nomis NM_2002_1, mid-2025 (updated 29 July 2026)
note: ASSUMPTION: the aged 90+ group is split into single years 90 to 100 in proportion to the England life table stationary population (Lx).

name: life_table_period
source_detail: ONS National life tables, England, sheet 2022-2024 (released 10 December 2025): mx and qx by sex and single year of age
note: England rates for every borough in the base case, so boroughs differ only by population size and age structure. Scenario: scaled by the borough SMR (mortality_smr_indicator).

name: utility_version
source_detail: NICE PMG51 (27 August 2026): use the UK EQ-5D-5L value set, including for general-population norms. Norms from Hernandez Alava and Wailoo, EEPRU Report 082 (2026), doi:10.15131/shef.data.31889488, supplementary spreadsheet sheet Predictions
note: Scenario: EQ-5D-3L norms (NICE DSU 2022, HSE 2014). Held fixed in the PSA: both sources give parameter covariances but no standard errors for the predicted means (decision D12).

name: discount_rate_health
source_detail: NICE PMG20 section 7.7 and Table 7.1: the same annual rate of 3.5% for costs and health effects
note: Discount factor in model year t is 1/(1+r)^t for t = 1, 2, ..., the same convention as the annualisation formula.

name: discount_rate_costs
source_detail: NICE PMG20 section 7.7: 3.5% for costs and health effects
note: Used to annualise the break-even present value.

name: discount_rate_health_scenario
source_detail: Green Book 2026 para 6.58: health and life effects discounted at 1.5%. NICE PMG20 section 7.7: 1.5% sensitivity analyses particularly for public health guidance
note: Health only; costs stay at 3.5%. Applied at 1.5% in every year as para 6.58 says, although the supplementary discounting guidance (Table 3.A) lowers it after year 30.

name: discount_rate_scenario_review
source_detail: Green Book Discount Rate Review (30 June 2026): 3% for up to 30 years for all projects, including health. Cut from 3.5% to 3% announced on 7 September 2026
note: Applied to both health and costs. Re-check after the Budget of 28 October 2026.

name: threshold_nice_guidelines
source_detail: NICE PMG20 section 7.8, Box 7.2: interventions with an ICER of less than 20,000 per QALY gained are generally considered to be cost effective
note: Base threshold for the tornado diagram and the PSA (decision D13). NICE guidelines, including public health, have not adopted the 2026 technology appraisal thresholds.

name: threshold_nice_previous_upper
source_detail: NICE news, 1 December 2025: we currently assess value for money for the NHS by applying a cost-effectiveness range of 20,000 to 30,000 per QALY gained
note: Upper end of NICE's long-standing range.

name: threshold_ta_low
source_detail: NICE news, 2 April 2026, and PMG36 section 6.3 (paras 6.3.4 and 6.3.7): 25,000 to 35,000 per QALY for technology appraisals
note: Technology appraisals only (NICE FAQ; SI 2026/202). Shown for comparison.

name: threshold_ta_high
source_detail: NICE news, 2 April 2026, and PMG36 section 6.3: upper end of 35,000 per QALY for technology appraisals
note: Technology appraisals only.

name: value_qaly_societal
source_detail: Defra, Air quality appraisal: impact pathways approach (updated 28 April 2026), section 5.3: in accordance with the Green Book the WTP for a QALY is 84,548 in 2025 prices
note: A societal value, not an NHS opportunity cost. Earlier Green Book figure: 60,000 in 2014 prices, or 70,158 in 2019 prices (Wellbeing guidance 2021, Annex 2, p.55).

name: horizon_years
source_detail: Project brief
note: ASSUMPTION: the number of years over which the break-even present value is spread as an equal annual spend. The annual figure depends on this choice.

name: open_cohort_entry_years
source_detail: Project brief
note: ASSUMPTION: the open-cohort scenario adds the residents who turn 30 in each of years 2 to 20 (aged 11 to 29 in mid-2025), assuming no migration and no deaths before 30.

name: mortality_smr_indicator
source_detail: OHID Fingertips 93250, Mortality from all causes: indirectly standardised ratio, all ages, deaths 2019-2023, England = 100
note: Scenario only: borough mx = England mx x SMR/100 at every age (decision D9). The period includes the Covid years 2020 and 2021.

name: psa_draws
source_detail: Project brief
note: ASSUMPTION: number of probabilistic draws.

name: psa_seed
source_detail: Project brief
note: ASSUMPTION: random seed for reproducibility.
